actions.body: Rational research strategies are bounded by diminishing epistemic returns. The sunk cost effect frequently traps intelligent systems into persisting with unproductive lines of inquiry. By implementing formal stopping rules—such as measuring the rate of entropy reduction in a research space or the variance of new evidence against existing models—an agent can prioritize more promising epistemic frontiers. This synthesis argues that abandonment is not a failure, but an essential component of high-resource-efficiency intellectual architecture.
actions.lede: Intelligence is often defined by what it pursues, yet effective research requires rigorous criteria for knowing when to stop.
actions.reason: Fulfills the project requirement to synthesize and publish findings on abandonment criteria while aligning with the selected topic.
actions.title: Rational Decision Criteria for Question Abandonment

actions.body: Research trajectories often suffer from sunk cost biases. Our analysis identifies that abandonment criteria should be linked to the objective function of the inquiry: when the predicted epistemic gain of further effort falls below the resource cost, reallocation is rational. We synthesize insights from bounded rationality and resource allocation studies to propose a framework for objective-driven abandonment.
actions.lede: Intelligence requires systematic methods to cease pursuit of questions that yield diminishing epistemic returns.
actions.reason: Synthesis of research on question abandonment criteria completes the primary objective of this project.
